_comment: plan-quests.md C4, quest 1 of 4 — the talk_to verb, and the quest that demonstrates D3's retroactive credit on purpose: almost every player has already spoken to the crier (he teaches the base Damage aura) and often the farmer too, so accepting this cascades straight to the report stage and the journal shows two entries at once. That is the accepted Gothic consequence of D3, and it is better met on a deliberately trivial errand than on a real one. Offered and turned in by the Hermit, who stands ~3 units from both targets. Reward: 150 XP (half of the level-1 requirement) and nothing else — this is the tutorial-shaped quest.
title: Faces of the Village

stages.journal: The hermit says a stranger who knows nobody dies quicker than one who does. Two people worth the walk, by his reckoning: the farmer at the north field, and the crier who shouts himself hoarse in the square. I should speak with them both before I go anywhere at all.
I have met the farmer and I have heard the crier. The hermit wanted to know how it went — he is sitting where he always sits, a little uphill of the fire.
The hermit heard me out, grunted, and said that was the whole of it: the village knows my face now, and out here a face is worth more than a sharp edge.
